look_here_first: Look for obvious individual hairs before looking at the flower. Prairie petunia is conspicuously long-pilose on stems, leaves and especially leaf margins, and its flowers are axillary and nearly sessile. That shaggy/ciliate look separates it from finely pubescent R. drummondiana and mostly glabrous terminal-flowered R. ciliatiflora.

lookalikes.differences: Ruellia drummondiana: Both have axillary nearly sessile purple flowers; R. humilis has conspicuous long hairs/ciliate margins, while R. drummondiana is short-finely pubescent and uniquely has only 2–4 seeds per capsule. Ruellia ciliatiflora: R. ciliatiflora is much less hairy and carries flowers in conspicuous peduncled terminal/upper-axillary cymes. Ruellia metziae: R. metziae tends toward terminal pedunculate pale/white flowers and lacks the strongly long-pilose prairie-petunia look.
